questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Law Faculty at UvA is among the best in Europe which was important to me. Also, Amsterdam is just such a nice city to live in which was equally important.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Months before arrival UvA sets up a student e-mail where all the relevant information is provided.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All necessary information was provided on the e-mail and the dedicated staff were also super helpful during the entire stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding housing in Amsterdam on the private market is super tough. If you are not offered student housing through the university lottery-system, I would advice you to start looking immediately. Be aware that there are a lot of scammers trying to exploit foreigners.
I mainly used
https://kamernet.nl/en
,
https://www.kamer.nl/en/
and also Facebook groups. I found my room on Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nothing particular. It is easy getting around Amsterdam on bike and thus easy to get to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything needed to register for courses is provided in due time. The registration process was intuitive and convenient and I did not face any problems during the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The staff at UvA are always super helpful. Also, the UvA web-page is also helpful to get information on all relevant questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I signed up for. If you do not get all the courses that you registered for, there is an "eftertilmeldingsperiode" where you can perhaps get the course anyways. Many of the other students got the courses they wanted that way.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Nothing particular - as I said, it was fairly easy and straight-forward. The list of courses for exchange students can be found here:
https://coursecatalogue.uva.nl/xmlpages/page/2023-2024-en/search-programme/programme/7324

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general, the courses were very theoretical and harder than at UCPH. Be aware that there are a lot of mandatory course materials and the work load was a lot higher than at the UCPH. The level of the exams appeared to be a bit easier than at UCPH. In almost all my courses, there were weekly hand-ins which was often a bit stressful.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at UvA is very interactive and encourages students to participate actively throughout the course. Generally, the courses are more "academic" and not as practical as what I am used to from UCPH. It took some time to adapt and get used to it, but it was a nice change and provided interesting insights.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Law, Advance Private Law in Context, Consumer Rights in the Digital Single Market, International Commercial Arbitration and European Contract Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It depends on preferences. The first three mentioned courses were very theoretical and academic, whereas the last two were more practically minded. However, personally I enjoyed and would recommend both International Commercial Arbitration and Advanced Private Law in Context.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I signed up for a sports association through the University which was a bit expensive. Also, it is a good idea to rent a bike upon arrival. Course materials are often uploaded in Canvas, and it is thus not necessary to buy all the books which was nice.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam is an expensive city to live in. Rent on the private market was way more expensive than expected. Groceries and stuff like that is around the same price as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Students were encouraged to sign up for different clubs. Some of my fellow students signed up for creative classes through the university. Personally, I signed up for a tennis class through the University which was very fun!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining a club or signing up for an activity. As previously mentioned, the work load is very high at UvA, and I found it important to get a break from studying every once in a while. Also, Amsterdam is super rich in culture and has some amazing museums.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: One of my favourite activities was just walking around the city. The city is so beautiful - especially during the week where there are less turists (the amount of turists can be a bit overwhelming in the weekends). I would recommend to visit the Van Gogh museum, but tickets are often sold out and needs to be booked in advance.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the Dutch people are very outgoing and friendly. Amsterdam is a very international city with many different cultures. Almost everyone speaks fluent English making it easy to communicate. All in all, I did not experience any issues adjusting to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mainly followed the MA programme "European Private Law" and the programme consisted of many different nationalities, and therefore I did not really get to meet many local students. However, the few I got to meet were very friendly. Always a good conversation starter to mention the bad weather (which is often even worse than in Denmark!).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Since the class-rooms were often very international with many different nationalities, there were many different cultures. However, I did not really experience any problems with cultural difficulties. All of the students were super friendly and nice regardless of nationality or culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Dutch people are in many ways very much like the Danes, and it was therefore easy to get along with the locals. I really liked the biking culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware that the work load is a lot higher than at the UCPH which surprised me. It is important to be up-to-date on the readings as it will be difficult to catch up later. There is no time off for exam preparations. Also, it is common that you will have to do weekly assignments in all courses that need to be handed in. 

2. If you are not offered student housing through the university, start looking for a room as soon as possible. Many students have to give up coming to Amsterdam because they simply did not start searching in due time. 

3. If you have the option, I would advice to mix the courses between BA and MA courses, as MA courses appear to be much harder than the BA courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UvA has really strict language requirements for being enrolled and you have to take a language test. However, if you take the 0 ECTS course "Legal English" at UCPH and has gotten 10 or higher in English A in High School, you can be exempt from the language requirements.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My English skills have improved both written and orally which is really nice. But more important, it is super rewarding getting to work with people from other cultures that you would otherwise not be able to. It is also a great (and difficult) personal challenge moving to a new city and having to leave friends and family for a while.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Before the exchange, the biggest challenge was without a doubt finding housing which almost felt like a full-time job. 

During the exchange, it was challenging to adapt to another way of teaching than what I am used to. Since there were no time off before the exams, it was very difficult and stressfull to prioritize the time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I think it is important to flag, that an exchange in Amsterdam is not a "vacation". The courses are intense and the work loads are very high. However, if you like facing new academic challenges, I would highly recommend going to Amsterdam.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
